sampling_model.design: One random sample of \(n\) independent bounded-window vectors; causal randomness and inferential sampling randomness are kept distinct.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one binary vector in \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The focal treatment is \(X_{-\gamma}\); the causal estimand compares two interventions while fixing the common possible-parent set \(Z\) at \(z\).
sampling_model.overlap: The collapse and strict-separation results use a strictly positive observed-window law; the general sharp compiler, empty-fiber certification, and confidence-fiber program permit probability-simplex boundary cells.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The multinomial vector \(p\) is estimated by \(\widehat p\); all causal endpoints and same-SCM pairwise contrasts are reoptimized over one simultaneous rational box-simplex region.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their controlled-effect theorem identifies the micro CDE by the conditional-mean adjustment contrast when the outcome is in no nontrivial directed cycle and has no bidirected edge to a directed ancestor.
Their response-function construction turns one specified discrete causal model into a polynomial program and obtains numerical valid bounds converging to sharpness.

Their causal-order linear program optimizes counterfactual queries over arbitrary masses on complete deterministic response signatures consistent with the supplied order and reconstructs attaining SCMs.
Proposition 3.1 preserves a canonical-domain linear program by pushing an unrestricted simplex mass to equivalence cells and selecting one raw representative per cell for the reverse lift.
Their bounded-segment theorem decides identification in one known periodic bounded-lag ADMG by cutting repeated hedge states.
Their PAG procedure gives sound analytical bounds at least as tight as natural bounds and shows that several graph representatives may remain necessary.
Their covering-collection construction gives uniformly valid minimum-average-volume confidence regions for a multinomial parameter.
Their root-cause method compares identified direct effects under an acyclic causally sufficient summary graph.
Their real-quantifier-elimination algorithm separates combinatorial and algebraic complexity in polynomial count, degree, coefficient height, and variable blocks.

body.tldr: A finite binary process is observed through a bounded window and a lag-abstracted directed and bidirected summary graph. The paper deliberately admits directed effects only at positive lags through \(L\), a restriction suited to delayed actuation or transmission at the sampling resolution; bidirected dependence may span any two summary-compatible time points in the observed \(H\)-window and is not bounded by \(L\). The sharp controlled-micro-direct-effect envelope is the attained extrema of a finite union of raw semi-Markovian response-function polynomial programs. A total exact certifier returns branchwise incompatibility certificates for an empty refinement fiber or isolated algebraic endpoints and attaining SCMs for a nonempty fiber. The envelope collapses to the Ferreira--Assaad adjustment functional and is strictly narrower, on a relative-open temporal-instrument family, than one internally defined complete temporal-order SCM comparator whose common latent selects arbitrary complete response tables. Every refinement embeds in that comparator by parent padding and latent bundling. Four rational primal--dual endpoint ledgers and an exact interior ledger support the strict comparison, while a simultaneous multinomial region supports tie-aware inference. The first-class open question concerns factorization-safe reduction of the graph-aware raw programs.

project_justification.gap: Existing summary-graph work identifies micro controlled direct effects only on sufficient graphical regimes; existing automated bounds take one fixed graph; existing order-only quotients use complete response-signature masses and do not preserve nonlinear independent-edge-latent product images.
project_justification.niche: The deliberate positive-directed-lag bound makes the full-time refinement set finite while leaving summary-compatible bidirected lags unrestricted inside the observed window. Binary canonical response functions make each fixed-refinement image semialgebraic, and the single maximal temporal-order common-latent model supplies a coherent graph-free outer comparator.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sharp unquotiented compiler and a total exact certifier, proves the point-identification reduction, and embeds every refinement into the complete order-only comparator by padding unused parents and bundling independent latents. Explicit rational graph-aware and complete-signature primal tables, pointwise dual inequalities, and an interior response-matrix ledger certify relative-open strict tightening. One multinomial event is propagated through all queries and contrasts, while factorization-safe quotienting remains an explicit equality-or-separation question.

body.related_work: Ferreira and Assaad (2026, Theorem on controlled micro direct effects) provide the summary-graph query setup and the adjustment expression recovered by the collapse theorem, but leave sharp sets outside their sufficient regime untreated. The absence of instantaneous directed arrows and the directed-lag bound \(L\) are deliberate restrictions of this paper, not assumptions attributed to Ferreira--Assaad or Jahn--Karnik--Schulman; they model delayed causal transmission, while bidirected lags remain unrestricted within the observed window. Duarte et al. (2024, Propositions 1--2 and Algorithm 2) provide the canonical response-function and polynomialization method adapted within each refinement; the total exact real-algebraic layer adds branchwise incompatibility certificates, endpoint isolation, causal-size bounds, and decoded SCM witnesses. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025, Propositions 1--2) show that a known bounded-lag periodic ADMG can be cut to a finite segment for identification; their work informs finite-window reasoning but is not the source of the present positive-directed-lag restriction or a theorem-level extension target. Rossetto and Antonucci (2026, theorem on the reduced linear program and its Appendix proof) motivate the comparator over arbitrary masses on complete response signatures consistent with a causal order. The comparator is specified here as one maximal temporal-order graph: every vertex has a deterministic table on all strictly earlier vertices and one finite common latent selects the full tuple of tables. A refinement SCM embeds by padding unused parent arguments and bundling all independent refinement latents; unrestricted common-latent mass is never assigned to a sparse graph with missing bidirected edges. Choe et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1) also quotient a linear program over an unrestricted signature simplex. Their reverse lifts need not lie in the explicitly defined push-forward family \(\overline{\mathcal P}_{G,\mathcal J}^{\mathrm{fac}}\), which retains independent overlapping edge-latent products. Evans (2016, Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 7.4) motivates retaining latent-margin structure beyond displayed ADMG constraints, and Evans (2021, Theorem 6.4) shows how hidden-variable dependence constructions can exploit nonlocal graph structure. Geiger and Meek (1999) and Basu, Pollack, and Roy (1996) supply the exact-elimination and complexity ancestors. Bellot (2024, Propositions 3--5) demonstrates that partial graphical information can improve graph-free bounds but does not give the temporal micro-CDE strictness region. The temporal-instrument certificate gives graph-aware endpoint masses and dual vectors, the complete eight-row order-only response tables and two pointwise comparator inequalities, and the rank-seven positive interior ledger needed to reproduce all four extrema and the relative-open comparison. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, Theorem 1) motivate whole-multinomial coverage, while Assaad, Ez-Zejjari, and Zan (2023, Proposition 7 and Theorem 1) supply the downstream direct-effect root-cause comparison made uncertainty-aware by the same-SCM tie rule.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact quotient push-forward \(\overline{\mathcal P}_{G,\mathcal J}^{\mathrm{fac}}\) preserves the raw image by construction, but it does not itself reduce the latent product parameterization. Computational reduction replaces that induced family by branchwise unrestricted quotient-simplex masses, and this replacement may enlarge the image. The mandatory first test fixes \(H=L=1\), \(A_0\leftrightarrow B_0\leftrightarrow C_0\), \(A_{-1}\to C_0\), and the singleton controlled effect of \(A_{-1}\) on \(C_0\); failure must be recorded by an algebraic quotient point and an exact nonmembership certificate and forces the unquotiented route.
body.honest_scope: The paper deliberately excludes instantaneous directed effects and directed lags beyond \(L\); it places no \(L\)-bound on bidirected lags, which may span the full observed \(H\)-window. The envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself is not asserted to be connected. The finite-window model is the target, so no stationarity or infinite-history reduction is assumed. Exact certification is worst-case singly exponential in the number of raw response-weight variables and is intended as a certificate engine, not a claim of polynomial-time scalability. It is total: an empty refinement fiber produces a refinement ledger and exact infeasibility certificate for every raw branch, whereas a nonempty fiber produces attained algebraic endpoints and decoded SCMs. The order-only comparator is one complete temporal-order SCM class with arbitrary mass on a single common latent signature; every graph refinement embeds in it, but its unrestricted mass is not claimed to respect missing bidirected edges. The strictness neighborhood is relative to the positive laws having a nonempty summary-graph refinement fiber. The edge-latent-chain witness uses \(H=L=1\) and contains graph-aware primal and dual tables, complete eight-row order-only primal signatures with nuisance completions, two pointwise comparator dual inequalities, and an exact rank-seven positive interior witness. Equality of the raw and exact factorized push-forward images is a fidelity lemma; equality with the unrestricted quotient-simplex image, a factor-preserving selector, and the quotient-size bound remain open and must first survive the stated six-vertex kill test. When the refinement class is a singleton, the construction reduces to the known fixed-graph response program, and on the Ferreira--Assaad graphical regime it reduces further to their adjustment functional.
